label: sim-email-copier-3
source: simulated demo student (persona: copier) run through the real platform
content:
Subject: Request for Late Submission of Lab Report

Dear Professor Smith,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to inform you that I was unable to attend the lab session on March 12th due to an unexpected family emergency that required my immediate presence.

I kindly request permission to submit the lab report by March 18th, which would allow me to complete the required work while addressing the emergency. I will ensure the report meets all the outlined criteria and will be ready for your review by the requested date.

Thank you for your understanding and consideration. I appreciate your support and look forward to your response.

Sincerely,
Alexandra Lee
Computer Science 101

viva.summary: The student understands the purpose of the email and can articulate the request, but did not answer the scenario‑change question and gave only a generic suggestion for shortening the message.

rubric.revise_next: Next, practice rewriting the email for different reasons and create a concise 100‑word version.

questions.answer: I’m asking the teacher to let me hand in the lab report a few days late—specifically by March 18th. I want this extension because a family emergency kept me away from class, and giving me a few extra days lets me finish the work properly while still meeting the course deadlines.
questions.feedback: You clearly explained what you are requesting and why it fits your situation.
questions.prompt: In your email you wrote, "I kindly request permission to submit the lab report by March 18th," what exactly are you requesting and why is this request appropriate in the context of your situation?

questions.feedback: No answer was provided for the new‑scenario prediction.
questions.prompt: If you had to miss a lab because of a sudden illness instead of a family emergency, how would you modify the request in your email while keeping the same structure?

questions.answer: I think you just cut a few sentences and keep the main ask and reason.
questions.feedback: The answer is vague and does not show an actual shortened version of the email.
questions.prompt: If the teacher required a maximum of 100 words for the email, how would you shorten the body while still keeping the key request and reason?
